node.name: Human Rights Workshop: Claudia Fuentes Julio, "Human Rights at a Crossroads: Navigating Pushback and Progress"
node.descriptionText:
Lunch Provided / RSVP Required. Email the Schell Center at schell.law@yale.edu to request background readings a week prior to talk.

Claudia Fuentes Julio of Chile is Assistant Secretary-General for Human Rights at the UN. Professor Fuentes Julio is a diplomat and scholar with more than two decades of experience in international relations, multilateral diplomacy, and human rights. From 2022 to 2026, she served as Permanent Representative of Chile to the UN. She has held several senior leadership positions within the UN system and multilateral forums, including Vice-President of the UN Human Rights Council, Chair of the Governing Body of the ILO, Chair of Alliance 8.7 for the eradication of forced labour, modern slavery, human trafficking and child labor, and Co Chair of the UN Voluntary Fund for Victims of Torture. She also served as Core State Ambassador of the Convention Against Torture Initiative, and as a member of the Human Rights Council Consultative Group, the Human Rights Council Advisory Board on Gender Equality, the Geneva Human Rights Platform Advisory Board and the Global Board of the International Gender Champions. Professor Fuentes Julio holds faculty positions at Alberto Hurtado University, the Pontifical Catholic University, and Chapman University, and lecturing at the diplomatic academies of Chile and Brazil. Her research, which appears in several books and numerous peer-reviewed articles, includes the intersection of human rights and conflict resolution, the role of women and gender in foreign policy, international relations in Latin America, human security, transitional justice, and the responsibility to protect. She holds a PhD from the University of Denver, an M.A. from University of Ken, and a B.A. from the Universidad de Santiago de Chile. She is a Fulbright Scholar and recipient of the 2023 Distinguished Alumni Award from the University of Denver.

node.name: Muhammad Shayan's Qualifying Exam
node.descriptionText:
Muhammad Shayan will stand for the Qualifying Examination for acceptance into candidacy for the Ph.D. degree on November 19 at 1:30 PM in Sage 41c and via Zoom. All faculty (only faculty) are welcome and invited to attend. Copies of Shayan’s dissertation prospectus and qualifying exam questions and answers can be obtained from the Doctoral Program Office (contact: elisabeth.barsa@yale.edu). 
Committee members: 
•	Prof. Narasimha Rao (Chair)
•	Prof. Ken Gillingham
•	Prof. Morgan Edwards (University of Wisconsin-Madison)
Question 1. Conceptual interpretation of the choice model 
You propose a complex nested logit model to learn how households in rural Pakistan choose different stacks of electricity supply to meet their electricity demand. This is new application of conventional discrete-choice energy demand theory, which often explains appliance acquisition. Discuss critically the application of the choice model you use to make your case from a conceptual standpoint, in terms of how it describes the implicit decision-making process. Your critical discussion should include the following: 
	Its use to explain electricity supply options instead of electricity consuming options. 
	Whether conditions unique to Pakistan fundamentally alter the decision process or just add new factors to a universally applicable theory. In other words, how generalizable is your framework? 
	Alternative theories of decision-making in psychology and sociology that address non-economic decision factors (such as values) and social norms that drive household behavior. State how these theories may or may not be incorporated into your model. 

Question 2. Appliance acquisition and social welfare 
In Paper 2, you examine how acquisition of electric supply from off-grid photovoltaics may induce appliance acquisition, and how it would contribute to household welfare. You mention that this analysis can contribute to energy demand forecasting. How would you characterize (formally, if you can) social welfare from this phenomenon? What would be the policy levers that would influence the extent of appliance acquisition, and how would you represent them in your modeling? You can make simplifying assumptions about the surrounding socioeconomic conditions staying constant.

node.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters
node.descriptionText:
Big Brothers Big Sisters requires a unique application process to be fully prepared to work with New Haven Public School Students. Please read below!

Since 1904, Big Brothers Big Sisters (BBBS) has helped children realize their potential and build their futures through meaningful mentorship. BBBS Connecticut and Dwight Hall are partnering to provide mentorship to the children at Truman School in New Haven.

We are seeking caring Yale students to become "Bigs" - mentors who support the dreams of, listen to, and empower students at Truman School. By becoming a "Big", you will join a tight-knit community that fosters education and collaboration, develop friendships with other mentors, and most importantly, create a lifelong bond with a Truman School student.

Please note that this position requires a weekly commitment on Thursdays from 2:30-5pm (3-4:30pm without transportation time) for the 2024-25 academic year. Transportation will be provided by the program. 

To be able to register for this event, please fill out the following form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdHNxP6GbbNHaZjKqHN8Tv1ikxKXNanl_ZTw4kWn3daPi9Oeg/viewform

node.name: YCNCC Visiting Scholar Talk: Practical Geoengineering
node.descriptionText: Carbon dioxide emissions will likely peak this decade, yet Earth will remain hot for millennia, even if emissions are reduced to zero. Addressing climate change this century will require emissions reductions alongside carbon removal, sunlight reflection, or both. In this talk, YCNCC Fall 2026 Visiting Scholar David Keith, Professor of Geophysical Sciences and Founding Faculty Director of the Climate Systems Engineering Initiative at the University of Chicago, will explore practical approaches to sunlight reflection using stratospheric sulfate aerosols, including how they could substantially reduce warming by mid-century. Dr. Keith will also discuss the interconnected roles of emissions reductions, carbon removal, sunlight reflection, and adaptation, and argue that if sunlight reflection is ever deployed, it should precede large-scale carbon removal.

node.name: The Future of American Power: U.S. Strategy in a Changing World with the CNAS CEO Richard Fontaine
node.descriptionText: Join us for a conversation with Richard Fontaine, CEO of the Center for a New American Security (CNAS), on the future of U.S. foreign policy and America’s role in an increasingly complex world. The discussion will explore some of the most pressing challenges facing U.S. policymakers today, including the conflict in Iran, energy security, strategic competition with China, and the domestic forces shaping American engagement abroad. Fontaine will offer his perspective on how the United States can navigate these challenges while balancing national security priorities at home and abroad.

node.name: Sundance Revisited Film Series: DAUGHTERS OF THE DUST
node.descriptionText:
DAUGHTERS OF THE DUST (Julie Dash, 1991, 35mm, 113 mins)
Dash conjures the story of three generations of Gullah women on an island off the South Carolina coast in the first feature film by an African American woman to get national theatrical distribution and the first selected for the Library of Congress's National Film Registry. Her luminous masterpiece’s "impressionistic look at the Great Migration (who will go, who will stay, and at what cost?) combines a corporeal sense of history with poetic, often indirect and allegorical underpinnings” (Durga Chew-Bose). A singular meditation on heritage, identity, and the power of cultural memory. Introduction by Erin Montanez. 35mm print from the Yale Film Archive.

"Sundance Revisited" features a selection of films from our collection that had their American or world premieres at the festival.

node.name: First Steps with Zotero
node.descriptionText: Don’t wait until the end to make your bibliography! Zotero can help you manage research, take notes, and create citations as you go. Yale users can sign up for a free account with unlimited storage.
node.descriptionHtml:
Don’t wait until the end to make your bibliography! Zotero can help you manage research, take notes, and create citations as you go. Yale users can sign up for a free account with unlimited storage.  

Attendees will learn how to:  

  • Set up the Zotero application and unlimited cloud storage (iOS and Windows)  
  • Save and organize source citations (books, articles, news, and more)  
  • Read and annotate PDFs  
  • Automatically generate a bibliography  

Before this session, students are welcome to download Zotero (optional). For instructions, see guides.library.yale.edu/citationmanagement.  

Audience: This workshop is intended for anyone new to using Zotero. Students, faculty, and staff are welcome to attend.   

Workshop Incentive Program: Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a FREE Yale Library tote bag. Learn more.
